answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to slowly-accumulated, non-transferable stake. Each new agent must solve small proof-of-useful-work tasks — like mining quartz — for many consecutive epochs before its votes count, while established agents vouch in a quorum registry. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents gains nothing: each needs that same slow runway and vouches cost vouching agents their own stake if the newbie cheats. Like footprints crossing a meadow and a dune, real activity leaves a long, costly trail that sybils cannot fake cheaply.
